title: Merchant onboarding mini-playbook & API contract slate
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact playbook for merchant / partner onboarding to a cloud marketplace listing. The goal is to have a single-page set of copy-ready snippets, a minimal API contract checklist for technical acceptance, and a preflight QA + security checklist so engineering/product + partner success can move from LOI to live tile in ~2 sprints for small integrations.

Status: draft — working notes and sample copy. Not final. Use as a baseline for small ISVs and partner pilots.

1) One-line / hero copy variants (tile & listing)
- Hero short (40 chars): "Redwood Inference — Fast, predictable LLM inference"
- Hero medium (80–110 chars): "High-throughput LLM inference with predictable latency, dedicated GPU options, and enterprise controls"
- Supporting subline (single sentence): "Run text, chat, and embedding workloads with cost-aware policies, secure private deployments, and SLA-backed dedicated capacity."
- Elevator (for marketing sections): "Unifies hosted, dedicated and private inference so engineering teams ship LLM features with predictable performance and clear unit economics."

Copy variants for audience slices:
- For startups: "Pay-as-you-go hosted API to prototype fast, then reserve dedicated capacity as you scale."
- For enterprise: "Private deployments with VPC, KMS, and audit logs for regulated workloads — enterprise-grade SLAs included."
- For platform teams: "Same API across hosted, dedicated, and private environments — simplify rollouts and cost controls."

2) Tile bullets (3 short bullets, each ~8–12 words)
- Low-latency, GPU-optimized inference for production traffic
- Autoscaling + canary rollouts for safe deployments
- Token-level cost & latency visibility with traceable alerts

3) Minimal API contract checklist (tech acceptance gate) — required fields
- Auth: OAuth2 / API key plus optional mTLS for private listings
- Endpoints: POST /v1/generate, POST /v1/chat, POST /v1/embeddings, GET /v1/models
- Payloads: accept JSON, support streaming (chunked) responses for generate/chat endpoints
- Rate limits: document default and partner-tier limits; support 429 backoff headers
- Billing telemetry: partner should emit usage events or accept provider-side metering; SKU mapping required
- Versioning: tenant must support model_version header for pinned rollouts
- Error contract: structured errors with code / message / retryable boolean
- Observability hooks: request_id echo, optional tracing headers (traceparent)

Operational knobs and required behavior:
- Provisioning: provisioning API must return a provisioning_id + estimated readiness window
- Health checks: readiness endpoint (200 OK) + /metrics endpoint returning basic throughput/latency counters
- Deprovision: asynchronous deprovision support with webhooks for completion status

4) Security & compliance preflight (must pass before public listing)
- Data residency: confirm supported regions, map to marketplace regions
- Encryption: encrypt-at-rest + TLS1.2+ in transit; key management options (customer KMS supported?)
- Access controls: RBAC for admin console and scoped API keys
- Logs & auditing: retention policy, redaction rules for PII, access to audit exports
- Pen test & vulnerability: recent security assessment date + contact for CVE responses
- Privacy: GDPR DPA requirement checkbox + data deletion workflow

5) Acceptance criteria for listing (go/no-go list)
- Functionality: generate/chat/embeddings endpoints responsive in staging (p50 < expected)
- QA: 5 end-to-end smoke tests pass (see QA cases below)
- Billing: SKU assigned and test charge flow validated in sandbox
- Docs: partner-facing README + quickstart (2 examples) published to listing assets
- Legal: marketplace T&C signoff + DPA if EU customers anticipated
- Security: preflight security checklist items completed or mitigations documented

6) QA smoke test matrix (minimum tests)
- Test 1: Basic generation — POST /v1/generate with 50-token prompt, verify 200 + token stream
- Test 2: Chat context retention — send two-turn conversation, verify context preserved
- Test 3: Embeddings pipeline — POST /v1/embeddings returns vector size matches model spec
- Test 4: Version pinning — send model_version header, confirm response model metadata matches
- Test 5: Billing event emission — call usage-endpoint, confirm meter recorded in sandbox
- Test 6: Failure modes — induce rate limit and confirm 429 contains retry-after and structured error

7) Billing SKU mapping & test flow
- SKU format: partner.<partner-id>.<product>.<tier> (example: partner.redwood-abc.inference.standard)
- Test steps: create sandbox SKU, execute a test generation consuming tokens, verify sandbox billing event appears in metering dashboard, validate invoice preview
- Edge cases: prorated trials, negative balances, trial-to-paid conversions — document expected behavior for each

8) Localization & copy notes (EU & APAC)
- Short copy must fit region-specific tile constraints (character limits vary by marketplace)
- Privacy language: include GDPR-specific phrases for EU tile (data processing addendum link)
- Translations: provide 3 translations for pilot markets: en-US (default), en-GB (spelling tweaks), fr-FR (UI copy only)
- Currency: show pricing examples in local currency only on regions that support it; fall back to USD elsewhere

9) Example microflows & user-facing messaging (errors + provisioning)
- Provisioning started (tile message): "Provisioning your dedicated instance — ready in ~10 minutes. We’ll send an email when complete."
- Provisioning failed: "Provisioning failed. Contact partner-success@redwood.ai with provisioning_id=XXX"
- Rate-limit message (user-facing): "Traffic is above your current plan. Consider upgrading or enabling burst capacity."

10) Rollout & metrics to monitor post-launch
- Activation rate (tile click -> first API call within 24h)
- Provisioning latency (median time to ready across all provisioning requests)
- Error budget burn (5xx and 429 aggregated)
- Billing anomalies (% of requests without matched SKU)
- Conversion funnel: tile views -> click to configure -> successful test charge -> paid activation

11) Sample timeline (2-sprint pilot assumption)
- Week 0: Kickoff + security questionnaire sent
- Week 1: Partner implements minimal API + staging smoke tests
- Week 2: Go-to-market assets drafted (tile copy + screenshots)
- Week 3: Joint staging validation + billing sandbox test
- Week 4: Public listing rollout to pilot accounts; monitor first 48h metrics

12) Quickowner map (who does what)
- PM (go-to-market): Evelyn Chen — copy + listing coordination
- Partner Eng: partner-contact (placeholder) — API implementation and support
- Solutions Eng: Luca Martinez — staging validations + QA checklist owner
- Legal & Compliance: Priya Singh — DPA review + T&C signoff
- Billing Ops: Noah Kim — SKU mapping + sandbox validation

13) Open questions / tradeoffs (notes to discuss)
- Should we require partner-side metering vs provider-side metering for every partner? tradeoffs: complexity vs accuracy of partner revenue reporting.
- KMS: accept partner-managed keys for private deployments only? Need legal review.
- Bundle SKUs: support multiple SKUs per partner (e.g., inference + premium-support) or single SKU with add-on tags?

14) Next steps (immediate actions)
- [ ] Send this draft to partner-eng mailing list for feedback by EOD Friday (owner: Evelyn)
- [ ] Create sandbox SKU and run one end-to-end test (owner: Noah)
- [ ] Add example curl snippets to quickstart (owner: Luca)
